unpatched_known_rce_cve.title: Unpatched Known-Exploited CVE Present
unpatched_known_rce_cve.description: TRUE when the running firmware/build is affected by an unpatched CISA KEV-listed CVE for this platform (FortiOS CVE-2024-21762, PAN-OS CVE-2024-3400, Ivanti CVE-2023-46805/CVE-2024-21887, Citrix Bleed CVE-2023-4966). Covers both the auth-bypass/RCE chain and the memory-disclosure session-token-leak primitive. The assessor cross-checks the running build against vendor advisories and the CISA KEV catalog. SECURE value is false (a supported image patched for all applicable KEV CVEs); the exposure fires when true.

firmware_end_of_support.title: Firmware End-of-Support
firmware_end_of_support.description: TRUE when the appliance runs an end-of-support / end-of-life firmware image that no longer receives security fixes — meaning newly disclosed KEV CVEs will never be patched on this build. SECURE value is false (a vendor-supported image); the exposure fires when true.

days_since_last_firmware_update.title: Days Since Last Firmware Update
days_since_last_firmware_update.description: Number of days since the gateway firmware was last updated. Internet-facing VPN appliances are mass-exploited shortly after disclosure, so a stale patch cadence is itself an exposure proxy. SECURE state is a small value (recently patched); the exposure fires when the value exceeds the 90-day patch-currency threshold.

session_idle_timeout_minutes.title: Session Idle Timeout (minutes)
session_idle_timeout_minutes.description: Idle timeout (minutes) for an established authenticated VPN/admin session before it is terminated. A long or absent idle timeout widens the window in which a stolen session token (e.g. Citrix Bleed CVE-2023-4966) can be replayed. Fires when above a tight bound (>15 min). Grounded in FortiGate SSL-VPN 'set idle-timeout' / 'set admintimeout'; secure value is short (~5 min).

max_session_lifetime_hours.title: Max Session Lifetime (hours)
max_session_lifetime_hours.description: Maximum absolute lifetime (hours) of an authenticated session/token regardless of activity. Long-lived or never-expiring sessions let a hijacked token persist indefinitely after the leak, even post-patch. Fires when above a bounded maximum (>24h). Grounded in SSL-VPN 'set auth-timeout'; secure value is a bounded re-authentication interval.

session_monitoring_enabled.title: Active Session Monitoring Enabled
session_monitoring_enabled.description: Whether active VPN sessions are monitored for anomalous source/geo/parallel use and exported to SIEM so a hijacked session can be detected and revoked. Fires when monitoring is absent (is_false). SECURE value is true.

concurrent_session_limit_enforced.title: Concurrent Session Limit Enforced
concurrent_session_limit_enforced.description: Whether a per-user concurrent-session cap is enforced, constraining a hijacked-token attacker logging in parallel with the legitimate user and aiding detection of anomalous duplicate sessions. Fires when no cap is enforced (is_false). SECURE value is true.

mfa_enforced_for_vpn_login.title: MFA Enforced for VPN Login
mfa_enforced_for_vpn_login.description: TRUE when multi-factor (ideally phishing-resistant) authentication is enforced for ALL remote-access VPN logins with no exception groups. SECURE value true. Fires (insecure) when login is single-factor/password-only or MFA is optional/bypassable, so stolen, sprayed, or stuffed credentials alone grant External Remote Services access. Per CISA Phishing-Resistant MFA / NIST SP 800-63B AAL2+.

rate_limiting_or_lockout_enabled.title: Brute-Force Lockout / Login Throttling Enabled
rate_limiting_or_lockout_enabled.description: TRUE when account lockout / login throttling (non-zero lockout threshold + duration, bounded SSH grace time) is configured on the public VPN portal and admin interface. SECURE value true. Fires (insecure) when there is no lockout / unlimited attempts, allowing unblunted password spraying and credential stuffing against the public-facing login. Derived from admin-lockout-threshold/duration (FortiGate) or vendor equivalent.

failed_auth_alerting_enabled.title: Failed-Auth Alerting Enabled
failed_auth_alerting_enabled.description: TRUE when authentication events (including failures) are forwarded to a central SIEM/syslog with failed-auth burst alerting and anomalous-session-source alerting enabled. SECURE value true. Fires (insecure) when logging is disabled/local-only or no failed-auth alerting exists, so credential spraying and post-exploit reverse-tunneling go unnoticed.

vpn_auth_source.title: VPN Authentication Source
vpn_auth_source.description: Which identity store the VPN authenticates against. Secure values bind to a central IdP / directory / certificate CA enabling central MFA, deprovisioning and audit. Fires (insecure) on local_appliance_accounts, which permits shared/local accounts that bypass central MFA and lifecycle controls and are a leading valid-account abuse path. Derived from the authentication-backend integration.

vpn_ikev1_aggressive_mode_disabled.title: IKEv1 Aggressive Mode Disabled
vpn_ikev1_aggressive_mode_disabled.description: Attests that IKEv1 aggressive mode is disabled (IKEv2-only preferred, per NSA/CISA and NIST SP 800-77r1). IKEv1 aggressive mode transmits the PSK hash in a way that exposes it to offline cracking. SECURE value is true; the exposure fires when aggressive mode is still enabled (false). Assessor interprets the real config key for IKE version/mode (FortiGate phase1 ike-version / Cisco crypto ikev1 with aggressive mode).

vpn_cipher_suites_strong_only.title: Strong VPN Cipher Suites Only
vpn_cipher_suites_strong_only.description: Attests that weak encryption/integrity algorithms (DES, 3DES, MD5, SHA1) are removed from the accepted phase1/phase2 (and SSL-VPN) proposals in favour of AES-GCM/AES-256 and SHA-256+. Modelled as an interpreted boolean rather than a substring match on the raw cipher list. SECURE value is true; the exposure fires when weak ciphers remain accepted (false).

perfect_forward_secrecy_enabled.title: Perfect Forward Secrecy Enabled
perfect_forward_secrecy_enabled.description: Attests that Perfect Forward Secrecy (PFS) is enabled on the IPsec phase2, so a compromised long-term key cannot decrypt past/future sessions (NIST SP 800-77r1). SECURE value is true; the exposure fires when PFS is disabled (false).

strong_dh_group_enforced.title: Strong Diffie-Hellman Group Enforced
strong_dh_group_enforced.description: Attests that only strong Diffie-Hellman groups are accepted (DH group 14+/2048-bit or ECP group 19/20/21) and the weak groups 1/2/5 (768/1024/1536-bit) are not offered. Modelled as an interpreted boolean to keep polarity safe. SECURE value is true; the exposure fires when a weak DH group is still enforceable/offered (false).

min_tls_version.title: Minimum TLS Version
min_tls_version.description: Workspace-canonical minimum TLS version accepted on the SSL-VPN portal (GlobalProtect / FortiGate SSL-VPN / AnyConnect WebVPN / NetScaler Gateway). Secure value is 'tls1_2_or_higher' (prefer TLS 1.3); the exposure fires when SSLv3/TLS1.0/TLS1.1 are still accepted ('tls1_0_or_tls1_1_or_sslv3_accepted'), enabling protocol downgrade and on-path interception (NIST SP 800-52r2).

least_privilege_access_enforced.title: Least-Privilege Access Policy Enforced
least_privilege_access_enforced.description: Whether the VPN gateway enforces a per-user/per-group least-privilege access policy that restricts which internal services and subnets an admitted session may reach (granular dst/service-scoped firewall rules from the VPN zone into the trust zone, mapped to each group's actual need). SECURE value true: each admitted identity reaches only the internal resources it requires. When false, any admitted session can reach the whole internal network, enabling lateral movement (NIST SP 800-46r2).

permit_any_from_vpn_pool.title: Permit-Any Rule from VPN Pool
permit_any_from_vpn_pool.description: Whether a broad 'permit any-any' firewall rule exists from the VPN pool/SSL-VPN interface into internal trust zones, granting every admitted session flat reachability of the internal network. INSECURE value true: a permit-any rule collapses the segmentation the gateway is meant to enforce. Modelled as an interpreted boolean (secure value false, non-firing).

vpn_pool_to_trust_segmentation_enforced.title: VPN-Pool-to-Trust Segmentation Enforced
vpn_pool_to_trust_segmentation_enforced.description: Supporting context: whether network segmentation (VLAN/zone separation, internal microsegmentation, or a downstream segmentation firewall) constrains traffic originating from the VPN pool so that even a broadly-permitted session cannot freely pivot across the trusted zone. Defense-in-depth evidence alongside the per-user access policy; not itself the primary trigger.

management_ui_internet_exposed.title: Management Interface Internet-Exposed
management_ui_internet_exposed.description: TRUE when the web/CLI admin interface (HTTPS/SSH) is reachable from the internet/WAN (e.g. allowaccess includes https/ssh on the external interface, admin bound to 0.0.0.0). Internet-exposed admin panels are the primary entry point for appliance RCE/auth-bypass CVEs (Ivanti, Citrix, Fortinet, PAN-OS). SECURE state is false (admin bound to a management network, WAN admin disabled); fires when true.

default_accounts_removed_or_changed.title: Default Credentials Changed
default_accounts_removed_or_changed.description: TRUE when the factory default admin password has been rotated and no vendor backdoor/maintenance accounts use shipped defaults. Default vendor credentials remain a top remote-access compromise path against the public-facing login. SECURE value true; fires (exposure) when false — defaults still valid.

admin_access_ip_restricted.title: Admin Access IP-Restricted
admin_access_ip_restricted.description: TRUE when administrative access is restricted to trusted source IPs/CIDRs (e.g. FortiGate trustedhost, management ACL) rather than reachable from any source. Fires (exposure) when false — admin login served to arbitrary internet sources, enabling brute-force/default-credential attacks.

auth_events_logged.title: Connection & Auth Events Logged
auth_events_logged.description: Interpreted from the VPN gateway's logging configuration: VPN connect/disconnect and authentication events — both success and failure — are recorded. SECURE value is true (events logged); the exposure fires when false, meaning credential abuse and anomalous sessions leave no record.

external_siem_forwarding_enabled.title: Logs Forwarded to SIEM
external_siem_forwarding_enabled.description: Interpreted from the gateway's remote-syslog/log-forwarding configuration: connection and authentication logs are exported off-box to a central SIEM/syslog target (not local-only). SECURE value is true (forwarded); fires when false, because a compromised gateway can impair its own local logging to evade detection (ATT&CK T1562.008) when records never leave the device.

client_posture_check_enabled.title: Client Posture Check Enabled
client_posture_check_enabled.description: Whether endpoint health/posture evaluation (AV present, OS patch level, disk encryption — e.g. a Host Information Profile / host-check policy) is configured and runs before VPN tunnel admission. SECURE value is true; the exposure fires when posture checking is absent so any device with valid credentials is admitted into the trusted zone (NIST SP 800-46 Rev. 2).

vpn_ztna_posture_gating_enabled.title: Device-Compliance Gating Enforced
vpn_ztna_posture_gating_enabled.description: Whether the posture/compliance result is actually ENFORCED at admission — non-compliant or unmanaged devices are denied or quarantined rather than the check being advisory/log-only. SECURE value is true; fires when gating is not enforced, so an unmanaged or compromised personal host reaches the internal network.

managed_certificate_required_for_admissi.title: Managed Certificate Required for Admission
managed_certificate_required_for_admissi.description: Whether a managed/enterprise device certificate is required as part of admission, distinguishing corporate-managed endpoints from arbitrary personal hosts presenting only user credentials. SECURE value is true; fires when no managed-certificate requirement exists, allowing any credentialed device in.
